scope: Targeted official protocol, schema and SDK review for a personal manager communicating with remote agents. No model performance experiments or live agent messaging were performed.
source_policy: Pinned official GitHub text retrieved using the configured network proxy. SHA-256 values cover exact retrieved bytes. Application design recommendations are distinguished from protocol guarantees.
limitations: Documentation/schema inspection does not establish runtime conformance or deployment compatibility.

verified_claims: Interactive request handlers should acknowledge promptly; documented timeout is three seconds.
excerpts: We recommend calling `ack()` right away before initiating any time-consuming processes such as fetching information from your database or sending a new message, since you only have 3 seconds to respond before Slack registers a timeout error.

verified_claims: Default HTTP request-verification middleware validates request body, signature and timestamp; this middleware skips Socket Mode, which has a different authenticated transport.
excerpts: Checks the validity of `x-slack-signature`, `x-slack-request-timestamp`, and the request body data.

verified_claims: Events must be subscribed in app configuration; message subtypes include bot_message and message_replied.
excerpts: You can listen to [any Events API event](/reference/events) using the `event()` method after subscribing to it in your app configuration.

verified_claims: Slack acknowledgement is transport acceptance, not completion of long agent work; Bolt separates timely ack and lazy long-running processing.
Events do not require explicit ack() calls in these Bolt listeners, but FaaS listener processing still has a three-second deadline.
excerpts: Note that in the case of events, while the listener doesn't need to explicitly call the `ack()` method, it still needs to complete its function within 3 seconds as well.
`lazy: List[Callable]`: Responsible for handling time-consuming processes related to the request. The lazy function does not have access to `ack()`.

verified_claims: Multi-workspace apps require OAuth installation records and explicit bot/user scopes; use existing installation/state stores rather than inventing an authentication subsystem.
excerpts: Slack apps installed on multiple workspaces will need to implement OAuth, then store installation information (like access tokens) securely.

verified_claims: Bolt provides threaded messages and streaming helpers using channel and thread identities. These identities associate conversation; the application still needs authoritative task state.
excerpts: `thread_ts` | Sourced from the event payload. Falls back to the `ts` value if available.
If either `channel_id` or `thread_ts` cannot be sourced, the utility will be `None`.
